classical

jūglāns, jūglandis f.

noun, third declension

walnut; also the walnut tree

Lewis & Short: “a walnut; a walnut-tree”. The long ā in the nominative follows Traupman; it is not carried into the oblique stem. Varro, LL 5.102 derives the name from Jupiter’s acorn: ā Jove et glande jūglāns est appellāta. Pliny, NH 15.86 and 15.91: nucēs jūglandēs, with the green husk (calyx, calycis m.) and the woody shell (putāmen, putāminis n.).

See also nut, almond, peanut, peel.

SourcesLewis & Short: juglans · Lewis & Short: calyx · Lewis & Short: putamen

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 70–73.
